output_list.reason: The 'executeRoom' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When calculating 'halfFee', the value '20' is used as the divisor, which causes an overflow and can be exploited to make 'halfFee' extremely large, allowing the attacker to acquire additional funds owned by the smart contract.

The 'distributeFunds' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The for-loop starts from 0 and goes to 6, which can trigger overflow and wrap around to a very large value, causing the attack to gain more tokens than supposed to.
The 'random' function uses predictable inputs (block information and timestamp) to generate random numbers, which is unsafe and attackers can manipulate these random values to their favor.
The 'setCTO' function does not check the '0' address, allowing it to be set as a payable address, causing financial loss to the contract owner.
The 'setCEO' function does not check the '0' address, allowing it to be set as a payable address, causing financial loss to the contract owner.
